Thought: To determine the number of structural isomers for C6H12, I need to consider the possible arrangements of carbon atoms with the molecular formula C6H12. This formula indicates that the compound could be an alkene or a cycloalkane. I will list all possible structural isomers for both alkenes and cycloalkanes.

For alkenes (CnH2n), C6H12 can have different carbon chain lengths and double bond placements:
1. Hexene (1-hexene, 2-hexene, 3-hexene)
2. Methyl-pentene (2-methyl-1-pentene, 3-methyl-1-pentene, 2-methyl-2-pentene, 3-methyl-2-pentene, 4-methyl-1-pentene, 4-methyl-2-pentene)
3. Dimethyl-butene (2,3-dimethyl-1-butene, 2,3-dimethyl-2-butene, 2,4-dimethyl-1-butene)
4. Ethyl-butene (3-ethyl-1-butene, 3-ethyl-2-butene)
5. Trimethyl-propene (2,2,3-trimethyl-1-propene)

For cycloalkanes (CnH2n), C6H12 can form:
1. Cyclohexane
2. Methyl-cyclopentane
3. Ethyl-cyclobutane
4. Dimethyl-cyclobutane (1,1-dimethyl-cyclobutane, 1,2-dimethyl-cyclobutane, 1,3-dimethyl-cyclobutane)
5. Propyl-cyclopropane
6. Trimethyl-cyclopropane (1,1,2-trimethyl-cyclopropane, 1,2,3-trimethyl-cyclopropane)

Now, I will count the distinct structural isomers.
